聪明是解题的速度，智慧是选题与承受的能力。本手册把智商与情商放进「道、法、术、器: Cleverness solves problems quickly; wisdom chooses worthwhile problems and lives with the consequences. This manual places thinking and emotional awareness on one map—Dao, Fa, Shu and Qi—so techniques can mature into judgment.
处理信息的速度、广度与技巧。题目在那里，你解得快、解得巧、解得漂亮。它是术与器的: Speed, range and skill in processing information. Given a problem, you solve it quickly, elegantly and effectively: the peak of techniques and tools.
知道什么值得做、知道自己不知道什么，并且能与结果和平共处。它是道与法的开始。: Knowing what is worth doing, recognizing what you do not know, and living at peace with the outcome: the beginning of understanding and systems.

器可传，术可练，法可立，道可养。学从器入，用从道出。每个格子是一章，点开即读。: Tools can be shared; techniques practiced; systems established; understanding cultivated. Learn from the tools upward; act from understanding downward. Open any cell to read its chapter.
每个阶段的药都不同。聪明人最常犯的错，是在所有阶段都吃同一种药——再学一点新东西: Each stage calls for different practice. A common mistake is to prescribe the same remedy at every stage: learning one more new thing.

序、地图三章、两条路各四章、合一四章、附录两篇。通读约两小时，修炼以年计。: A preface, three map chapters, four chapters on each path, four on integration, and two appendices. Reading takes roughly two hours; cultivation takes years.

知之为知之，不知为不知，是知也。: To know what you know, and know what you do not know: that is knowledge.

共二十四题，分四组，约五分钟。每题描述一种做法，请按你实际做的频率作答，而不是你: Twenty-four questions in four groups, about five minutes. Each describes a behavior. Answer how often you actually do it, not whether you know what you should do.

我有一个固定的地方记录想法与笔记，并且每周至少回看一次。: I have one regular place for ideas and notes, and I review it at least once a week.
做重要决定时，我会把决定、理由和预期写下来，留待日后核对。: For important decisions, I write down the choice, reasons and expectations so I can check them later.
面对高风险的例行事务（重要邮件、汇报、签约），我有自己的核对清单。: For high-stakes routine tasks—important emails, presentations or contracts—I use my own checklist.
在反驳一个观点之前，我会先把对方的立场说到让对方认可「就是这个意思」。: Before challenging a view, I restate the other person’s position until they agree that I have understood it.
对预测性的判断，我习惯用具体的概率（比如「七成」）而不是「应该会」来表达。: When making predictions, I use a specific probability, such as 70%, rather than saying “it should happen.”
动手解决问题之前，我会先花时间用几种不同的说法重新定义问题。: Before solving a problem, I spend time defining it in several different ways.
无论心情好坏，我每周都会在固定时间复盘本周的决定与所学。: Whatever my mood, I review the week’s decisions and learning at a fixed time each week.
我会按「可逆/不可逆、影响大/小」给决定分级，并用不同的速度处理它们。: I classify decisions by reversibility and impact, and handle them at different speeds.
我有一份写下来的个人原则（「当……时，我……」），并且会定期更新。: I keep written personal principles (“When …, I …”) and update them regularly.
在讨论中我能坦然说「我不确定」或「我不知道」，不觉得有损自己。: In discussions, I can comfortably say “I’m not sure” or “I don’t know” without feeling diminished.
我能一边全力推进一个方案，一边真诚地承认它可能失败。: I can work wholeheartedly on a plan while honestly acknowledging that it may fail.
做判断时我会考虑五年后的后果，并愿意为长期的好处接受眼前的笨拙。: When judging a choice, I consider its consequences five years ahead and accept short-term awkwardness for long-term benefit.
我能用比「不爽」「还行」精确得多的词，说出自己此刻的情绪。: I can describe my current feelings with words more precise than “bad” or “fine.”
情绪升起时，我会先注意到身体的信号（胸口发紧、呼吸变浅），再决定怎么回应。: When emotion rises, I notice bodily signals—tightness in my chest or shallow breathing—before deciding how to respond.
我有记录情绪触发与反应的习惯，并能从中看到自己的模式。: I regularly record emotional triggers and responses, and can see patterns in them.
在重要对话中，我会先复述对方的意思并得到确认，然后再表达自己的看法。: In important conversations, I restate the other person’s meaning and check it before offering my own view.
表达不满时，我会说具体的行为和它对我的影响，而不是评价对方「是什么样的人」。: When expressing dissatisfaction, I describe the specific behavior and its effect on me instead of judging what kind of person someone is.
听到批评时，我能先谢谢对方并提问澄清，而不是当场辩护。: When criticized, I can first thank the person and ask clarifying questions instead of defending myself immediately.
我知道自己一天或一周里情绪最脆弱的时段，并且避免在那时做关系上的决定。: I know when I am most emotionally vulnerable during the day or week, and avoid relationship decisions then.
每周我都会主动为生活中重要的人做一件具体的「存款」（感谢、兑现承诺、认真倾听）。: Every week, I make a concrete “deposit” for someone important to me: specific thanks, a kept promise or attentive listening.
冲突之后，我会在二十四小时内主动发起修复，不论对方是否先动。: After conflict, I initiate repair within twenty-four hours, whether or not the other person moves first.
我清楚自己在压力下的核心模式（防御、讨好、控制、退缩），并能在它启动时察觉到。: I recognize my core stress pattern—defensiveness, pleasing, control or withdrawal—and can notice it starting.
在冲突中，我能持续把对方当作一个有恐惧和需要的完整的人，而不是「那个不讲理的人」: During conflict, I continue to see the other person as a whole human with fears and needs, rather than simply “the unreasonable one.”
被激怒时，我的声音和判断依然稳定——不是硬撑，而是愤怒没有占满我。: When provoked, my voice and judgment remain steady—not because I force them to, but because anger does not fill my entire attention.
招很多，心很空。短期极有效，长期很累也很孤独——会赢，但不会活。你知道如何让人同: Many moves, little inner direction. You may be effective in the short term yet exhausted and isolated over time: able to win, less able to live well. You know how to gain agreement, but perhaps not why you seek it.
满口道理，一到具体事就露怯。这一类常常把「看破」当成境界，其实是没有能力入局。回: Principles come easily; concrete action does not. What looks like having “seen through everything” may be an inability to engage. Return to tools and techniques: do something concrete, unglamorous and testable.
工具囤积症。收藏是学习的廉价替代品，让人有进步的幻觉。三个月内不学任何新东西，每: Collecting tools can become a cheap substitute for learning and create an illusion of progress. For three months, stop adding new material and practice just one technique each month.
制度完善，灵魂缺席。复盘按时做，日课天天打卡，但你已经忘了这一切是为了什么。定期: The routines are complete, but their purpose is absent. Reviews happen on time and boxes get checked, yet you have forgotten why. Step back regularly and ask what all this is for.
左下满，右上空: Strong thinking tools, thin emotional foundations
思考的工具和技法很多，而情绪、关系与心性那一侧稀疏。这是读这本手册的人最常见的形: Your thinking tools and techniques are well developed, while emotions, relationships and character receive less attention. This is a common pattern among this manual’s readers. Part III deserves priority: start with Chapter 8.
你对人的感知强于对事的分析——人人喜欢你，但你可能做不出足够清晰的决定，也容易被: You read people more readily than problems. People may like you, yet clear decisions can be difficult and you may be taken advantage of. Prioritize Part II: start with Chapter 4.
先选定一个笔记入口，开始写决策日志。三个月内不再学任何新框架。: Choose one place for notes and begin a decision log. Add no new frameworks for three months.
用情绪词汇表，每天命名一次；开始写情绪日记。三个月不学新的沟通技巧。: Use an emotion vocabulary and name a feeling each day; start an emotion journal. Add no new communication techniques for three months.
每月只练一式，从「停一下」开始。晚间复盘记下今天用了几次。: Practice one technique per month, starting with “pause.” Record how often you used it in your evening review.
每月只练一式，从「命名」开始。接受前几十次都会失败——事后想起来就算进步。: Practice one technique per month, starting with naming emotions. Expect early attempts to fail; even remembering afterward is progress.
建立三级复盘、分级决策，开始写原则手册。守法一年，不看心情。: Set up three levels of review, classify decisions and begin a principles manual. Follow the system for a year, regardless of mood.
建立关系账户、二十四小时修复规则、冲突协议。把「日省」放进晚间复盘。: Set up relationship accounts, a twenty-four-hour repair rule and conflict agreements. Include self-examination in your evening review.
教别人；去承担后果的位置；每季退一步问「这一切为了什么」。回到器，重新做学生。: Teach others; take a role where you bear consequences; step back each quarter to ask what this is for. Return to the tools and become a student again.
去最难的人和最想逃避的对话那里「事上磨练」。为一个人的成长负责。: Practice in real situations with difficult people and conversations you most want to avoid. Take responsibility for someone’s growth.
看手机前写下：今天最重要的一个判断是什么？最可能激起我情绪的人或事是什么？我今天: Before checking your phone, write: What is today’s most important judgment? Who or what is most likely to stir my emotions? What kind of person do I want to be today—in one word?
停下来，用词汇表里最准确的那个词命名当下的情绪，再问它替哪个需要说话。记进情绪日: Pause, name your present feeling with the most precise word you can, and ask which need it speaks for. Record it in your emotion journal.
记一个决定：是什么、为什么、预期什么、多大把握（百分数）、何时核对。小决定也可以: Record a decision: what, why, expected outcome, confidence percentage and review date. Small decisions count too.
经典或一本真正的好书，十五分钟。一书未完，不看他书。写一句今天读到的最重要的一点: Read a classic or a genuinely good book for fifteen minutes. Finish one before starting another. Write one sentence about today’s most important insight.
今天哪个判断我会改？哪次互动我后悔或欣慰？学到了什么？——为人谋而不忠乎？与朋友: Which judgment would I revise? Which interaction do I regret or appreciate? What did I learn? Was I conscientious in helping others, trustworthy with friends, and practicing what I learned?
决策日志与情绪日记。找模式，不找错。: Read your decision log and emotion journal. Look for patterns, not faults.
关系账本上最久没有存款的那个人，本周给他存一笔——具体的感谢、兑现的承诺、一次认: Find the person who has gone longest without a deposit in your relationship ledger. Offer specific thanks, keep a promise or listen attentively this week.
与一个人进行一次不少于三十分钟、不带议程、真正在听的谈话。: Talk with someone for at least thirty minutes without an agenda, and truly listen.
为你本周最坚定的一个看法写一段反方陈述，写到你觉得「好像也有道理」为止。: Write the opposing case to your strongest conviction this week until you can honestly say, “That has a point too.”
回顾这周用了几次，效果如何。已经开始自动出现了吗？: Review how often you used it this week and how it worked. Is it beginning to happen automatically?
下周唯一最重要的一件事: Next week’s single most important thing
停止收集，选三件用满三个月: Stop collecting; use three tools for three months
每月一式，练到不用想: One technique per month, until it becomes natural
让好判断不依赖好状态: Make good judgment less dependent on your mood
教、负责、退一步；回到器重新做学生: Teach, take responsibility, step back; return to tools as a student
二十四题自测，看你在两条路上各站在哪一层。药要对症。: Twenty-four questions locate you on both paths. Choose practice that fits your starting point.
读完地图三章，从你薄弱的那一层读起。智商与情商可以并行读同一层。: Read the three map chapters, then begin at your weakest level. Read matching levels on the thinking and emotional paths together.
晨间三问、一次命名、一条决策日志、读一段、晚间复盘。三十分钟，每天。: Three morning questions, one named emotion, one decision entry, a passage to read and an evening review. Thirty minutes, every day.
